verses.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਭਾਇ ਪੇਖੈ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਬਿੰਬੁ ਚਕਈ ਜਿਉ ਨਿਸਿ ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਆਪਾ ਆਪ ਚੀਨਿ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: preet bhai pekhai pratibi(n)b chakiee jiau nis gurmat aapaa aap cheen pahichaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as Ruddy sheldrake looks amorously at her shadow during moonlit nights believing it to be her beloved, so does a Sikh of the Guru recognises the existence of his dear Lord within him and engrosses himself in it.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬੈਰ ਭਾਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਪਰਛਾਈ ਕੂਪੰਤਰਿ ਪਰੈ ਸਿੰਘੁ ਦੁਰਮਤਿ ਲਾਗਿ ਦੁਬਿਧਾ ਕੈ ਜਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: bair bhai pekh parachhaiee koopa(n)tar parai si(n)gh dhuramat laag dhubidhaa kai jaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as a lion sees his own shadow in the well and under the influence of his jealous feelings, considers it another lion and pounces upon it; similarly a Manmukh separated from his Guru due to his base wisdom is seen entangled in doubts.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗਊ ਸੁਤ ਅਨੇਕ ਏਕ ਸੰਗ ਹਿਲਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਰਹੈ ਸ੍ਵਾਨ ਆਨ ਦੇਖਤ ਬਿਰੁਧ ਜੁਧ ਠਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: guoo sut anek ek sa(n)g hil mil rahai savaiaan aan dhekhat birudh judh Thaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as several calves of cow live together in harmony, so do the obedient sons (Sikhs) of the Guru live in love and brotherhood with each other. But a dog cannot stand another dog and fights with him. (So do the self-willed persons are ever ready to pick up quarrels with each other).

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਚੰਦਨ ਅਉ ਬਾਂਸ ਬਿਧਿ ਬਰਨ ਕੇ ਦੋਖੀ ਬਿਕਾਰੀ ਉਪਕਾਰੀ ਉਨਮਾਨੀਐ ॥੪੯੩॥
verses.translit_en: gurmukh manmukh cha(n)dhan aau baa(n)s bidh baran ke dhokhee bikaaree upakaaree unamaaneeaai ||493||

en.bdb: The behaviour of Guru-conscious and self-conscious persons is like sandalwood and bamboo. Evil persons fight with others and destroy themselves as bamboos set themselves on fire. On the contrary, virtuous people are seen doing good to their companions.  (493)
